description: A single-panel line plot, labelled "(b)", giving the calculated diffusion coefficient of carbon in austenite as a function of temperature for two Nb-microalloyed medium-Mn low-density steels. The y-axis is labelled "Different coefficient (m²/s)" and carries a linear scale from 0 to 8×10⁻¹⁴ with ticks at every 1×10⁻¹⁴; the x-axis is "Temperature (K)" with labelled ticks at 673, 723, 773, 823 and 873 K. A legend identifies the black curve as "0.02Nb steels" and the red curve as "0.04Nb steels", and the on-plot annotation "C element" states that carbon is the diffusing species. Both curves rise steeply and non-linearly with temperature: each starts just below the 1×10⁻¹⁴ m²/s gridline at 673 K and ends between the 7 and 8×10⁻¹⁴ m²/s gridlines at 873 K. The two curves are nearly superimposed over the whole range, with the black 0.02Nb curve lying marginally above the red 0.04Nb curve and the small gap persisting to the highest temperature. The figure demonstrates that the higher-Nb (0.04Nb) steel has a slightly lower diffusion coefficient of C in austenite than the 0.02Nb steel over 673–873 K. Only panel (b) is present in the supplied image; the caption's panel (a) for Al diffusion is not shown, and no numeric data labels are printed on the curves.
measured_quantities: diffusion coefficient of C in austenite (m²/s)

observations.observation: The supplied image contains only panel (b); the caption's panel (a), which reports the diffusion coefficient of Al, is not present in this image.
Y-axis is labelled "Different coefficient (m²/s)" and runs linearly from 0 to 8×10⁻¹⁴ with tick labels at every 1×10⁻¹⁴.
X-axis is labelled "Temperature (K)" with labelled ticks at 673, 723, 773, 823 and 873 K.
The legend identifies the black curve as "0.02Nb steels" and the red curve as "0.04Nb steels".
The annotation "C element" printed on the plot states that the plotted diffusion coefficient is that of carbon.
Both curves start just below the 1×10⁻¹⁴ m²/s gridline at 673 K and rise steeply, ending between the 7 and 8×10⁻¹⁴ m²/s gridlines at 873 K.

The black 0.02Nb curve lies marginally above the red 0.04Nb curve at essentially every temperature, so the C diffusion coefficient is slightly higher in the 0.02Nb steel; no numeric data labels are printed on either curve.
The caption states that the diffusion coefficients of Al (a) and C (b) in austenite of the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels were calculated.
The citing text states that the diffusion coefficients were calculated with Thermo-Calc software using the TCFE10_MOBFE5 database over the temperature range 673-873 K.

The citing text states that Nb slightly decreases the diffusion coefficient of C in austenite because of the strong affinity between Nb and C, while the diffusion coefficient of Al slightly increases.

The citing text argues that, since growth/coarsening of κ-carbides is controlled mainly by long-range C diffusion rather than Al diffusion, the slower C diffusion caused by higher Nb content would decelerate nucleation and growth of κ-carbides.
The citing text additionally reports that the average κ-carbide size in 0.02Nb steels is consistently slightly larger than in 0.04Nb steels as aging temperature increases.

subfigures.description: Line plot of the diffusion coefficient of C in austenite vs temperature (673-873 K) for 0.02Nb steels (black curve) and 0.04Nb steels (red curve). Annotation "C element" marks the diffusing species.
